<!-- The manual of coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js: what it does stage by stage and the reason for each rule
     in force. Rewritten 2026-10-08 for the redesign built from process-engineering/batch-redesign.md, which holds
     the evidence and the cost of each new choice; the manual before it, with the history of every rule since
     2026-09-19, is in git at cd2393a08. -->

# The batch workflow script, stage by stage

The script runs one batch of the compile-ladder climb. Everything a batch changes lies between its `MANIFEST` and `END MANIFEST` lines, which the batch's generator writes (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-<N>/manifest/`). The rest of the script is the same for every batch. The practice it builds, and why, is `process-engineering/batch-redesign.md`.

In one paragraph: each rung's worker does its rung test first in its own seeded worktree. Its skeptic checks it and fixes what it finds, test first. A judge rules only on a fix the skeptic marks contested, on a rung it cannot fix, or on a worker's stop, and one repair round runs only on the judge's word. The gather lands the approved rungs on `main`. The merged-diff review and the gate run side by side. The commit stage lands the gate's tables, runs the quick microGPT walk check and pushes. The batch writes no skill text: the skill writer writes the skill from the batch's revival-change material after the landing, and a cold read follows ("After the landing: the coordinator's routing", step 4). Every agent runs on Opus but a judge's second ruling on the same rung or tree, which runs on Fable (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The roles").

## Gather

The gather composes one local commit per approved rung on `main`; nothing is merged.

- **The order.** First, a rung goes after every rung it lands only with (`landsOnlyWith`), so that no commit on `main` holds a rung without the rungs it needs: in climb batch 17 the old rule, which compared lines across files, put rung L's `2b1cd8e63` before rung W's `743eb5286`, and that commit alone fails `LibraryOverloadFamilies.fss:37` (`reviews/batch-17-review.md`, finding 2). Then the rungs that share a file go in the ascending order of their lowest edited line in that file, so that a later hunk does not shift lines a landed record cites; a line is compared only with a line of the same file, and rungs that share no file keep the manifest's order. Where two files order one pair both ways, the pair keeps the manifest's order. Any `file:line` a record cites that an earlier hunk shifted is re-anchored by symbol. Tests cite the specification by section, never by line, so no test is re-anchored.
- **Each rung.** Its net diff is applied with `git apply --3way --index`. A conflict in unrelated regions is resolved by hand; one in the same logic is returned, not guessed. Its files are written from the journal where the branch lacks them, by the commands the brief renders per rung. For a repaired rung, `REPORT.md` and `record.md` are always rewritten from the repair round's texts.
- **The record folded.** The FACTS entry under its area. A ledger note that adds a fact through `ledger.py note`. A change to what a row says (its claim narrowed, a half fixed, its test promoted or renamed, its notes at the limit) through `ledger.py rewrite N FILE`: the whole line, stating the gap as it stands now, not its repair history. A note refused for length goes in so, with the notes cut back; none is left out. New rows through `ledger.py add FILE --section TITLE`, each `NEW-<rung>-<n>` placeholder replaced with its number everywhere the rung's files and tests cite it, before the rung's commit. The handover line, in the batch's `RECORD.md`, "Handover lines" (the old handover file is retired into PLAN's first section, which the coordinator keeps). The rung's "Revival change" section is folded into no file: both its parts are copied, word for word, into the batch's `RECORD.md` (below), and nothing is written under `.claude/`. Through batch 13 the gather folded each entry into the skill's `revival-changes.md` as the rung wrote it, and the cold reader that followed made a question's handle findable instead of deleting it: that is how the coordinator's agenda reached the skill (`reviews/skills-agenda-audit.md`, "How it got there").
- **Corrections still owed.** The skeptic's `leftForGather` items. Each sentence of the specification a rung lists as made false and did not edit, corrected to what the code does, each clause checked against its code line. Batch 8's gather saw rung Q's Appendix I Effect false and let it stand, and in batch 9 no stage saw the one rung K made false. Each took a review judge and a repair, 0.53M and 0.39M (`reviews/batch-8-review.md`, section 5; `reviews/batch-9-review.md`, section 6).
- **Text mismatches.** A text mismatch the decisions do not settle is filed, not blocking ("Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect", item 4).
- **Items for the curator.** The gather puts every item a rung, skeptic or judge returned into `PLAN.md`, under "Pavol's answers, in the order they are needed" when work waits on it, else under "Off the path, parked".
- **After the rungs.** One commit closes each row a landed rung fixed (`ledger.py close N --commit HASH --test NAME`, then `ledger.py landing-check BASE`, which fails on any finding, also one the base already had; each is cleared through `rewrite`, `close` or `note`, or the entry reworded, before the commit). One commit writes the batch's `RECORD.md`, once, last: the order and why, each rung's commit, the rows opened and closed, each skeptic's fixes and the contested rulings by commit, the rungs that did not land, the points to report, where each item for the curator went, and last, under "Revival changes, for the skill writer", each landed rung's "Revival change" section, both parts word for word.
- **The specification's PDF.** When the gather builds the specification to check its text, it builds it once, on the text after the last edit under `Specification/`, and keeps the PDF at `tmp/gather/fortress-batch-<N>.pdf` in the main tree, which the commit stage takes ("Commit, and the push held", step 1).

A rung that did not land has its `REPORT.md` and `SKEPTIC.md` taken out of its branch path by path, its findings folded under "Not landed", and its new rows added. None of its source is applied.

Files are staged by an explicit list and `git diff --cached --stat` is read before each commit. A commit touching a path outside `explorations/` and `.claude/` carries a `historical:` line.

## Review beside the gate
## Commit, and the push held

The commit stage:

0. Starts the quick microGPT walk check in the background, unless an earlier attempt started it (`tools/mg-run.sh`, the quick pair, about a minute; P-30, "The check of microGPT under walk after a batch must take less than a minute."). It waits for the result before it returns. Unless both programs print `ALL PASS`, `microgpt-walk.1` is listed. It holds nothing.
1. Copies the gate's outputs into `compile-ladder/climb-batch-<N>/gate/` and the per-site list into place. It writes the landed figures into FACTS, numbers only, by `record.py set`, one call per entry, `FACTS-history.md` in the same commit: F-53's distance and count, from the two tables, and F-240's two stages' seconds. The distance stage's come from `distance.txt`'s `#seconds` and `#machine` lines. The count stage's table records none, so its seconds are the file times of the stage's own folder in the gate's log, from `checker-count/javac.txt`, written at its start, to `run.txt`, written last: 152 s at climb batch 23's gate, where the gate's call times gave about 155 s. Left to the coordinator, F-240 stood false at five landings running (`reviews/batch-23-review.md`, finding 3; `reviews/batch-22-review.md`, finding 4). If a landed commit changed `Specification/`, it copies the gather's PDF to `Specification/fortress.pdf` where the gather kept one and no commit after the gather's head changed `Specification/`, and builds the PDF once otherwise. In climb batches 23 and 24 the gather built the specification and removed its build, and the commit stage built it again on the same text, about 1.6 and 1.7 minutes; climb batch 24's record had the commit stage take the gather's build (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-24.md`, fork 7; `reviews/batch-23-review.md` and `reviews/batch-24-review.md`, finding 4).
   1a. Appends the repair runs and the paths no stage reads beside the summary, where the first gate's tables stand.
2. Checks every commit since the base: the skill's footer, no model identifier, and a `historical:` line where a commit touches the 2012 tree. Then it runs `git diff --name-only <base> HEAD -- .claude/`, which should print nothing. Each path it prints is listed as `skill-touched.N`, for the coordinator; it holds nothing.
3. Pushes `main` to `origin` and to `claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8` and `blinded-fable`, retrying a failed push up to four times (the protocol's hard rules).
4. Removes each rung's worktree without `--force`, with its ignored `tmp/` and the old code's caches folder. It keeps one git refuses, and names it, since it holds uncommitted work.

The push is held when any landed rung's worker or skeptic, the review, or a merged-tree repair reports a point with `holdsPush` true, or a malformed one: a step that cannot be undone or acts against a decision on record. The stage then pushes nothing, keeps the worktrees, and writes a "Not pushed." paragraph into `RECORD.md`; the coordinator pushes once the curator lifts it. Batch 5's push went out past an unlifted stop because nothing held it (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-5/RECORD.md`). A rung that did not land holds nothing.

## Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect

The curator's rule on gate reruns ends: "The same weighing of cost against what a rule protects applies to the other rules of the batch workflow." The rules in force from that weighing (batch N's review, `reviews/batch-N-review.md`, question 4):

1. **The review's judge may land and route.** A ruling whose every upheld finding is settled by tests and records only is `land`: no repair runs, and its steps go to the next batch. In batch N the repair and second review for two such findings held the batch 54 minutes after a green gate and cost about 1.0M.
2. *(The second review beside the commit: gone with the second review, 2026-09-29.)*
3. **The rungs' texts come from the run's journal**, by one `journal-text.py` command per file, never pasted into a brief. In batch N pasting them cost the gather 195K tokens of brief and 88K of copying. An agent after a compaction re-reads its own brief from its transcript.
4. **A text mismatch the decisions do not settle is filed, not blocking.** The text lands as the rung wrote it. The path that departs gets a ledger row and a gated `XXX` test asserting the text's rule, and the text's Appendix I entry names that row among its departures. Where no such test can show the departure, the path gets a gated test of today's behaviour, and the row says why: in climb batch 23 row 849's departure showed only in the one library's world, which only the gate's stages reach, and on the compiled path's repository the text's rule and the code both end in a static error (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-23/RECORD.md`, "Text mismatches"; `reviews/batch-23-review.md`, finding 8). The mismatch goes to the curator as `gather.N`. A mismatch the decisions settle is fixed on the side they settle.
5. **A rung does not run a stage its edit cannot move** (`STAGE_BLIND`, above). In batch N rung K, an interpreter-only edit, ran the checker count twice and read the landed total twice.
6. **A repair's new tests run together in one JVM**, one corpus at a time (`ONE_JVM=1 junit.sh`), since a test that passes alone can fail beside others. The next batch's gate runs them in the whole corpus.

## After the landing: the coordinator's routing

The coordinator's steps after a landing, in this order, each done whole:

1. The landing report to the curator.
2. The routing: every open row, record default and item for the curator filed with a batch or as a parked line of `PLAN.md`. Each is checked against POSITIONS and the notes `INDEX.md` lists before it is called open, put to the curator or briefed. In the same pass the routing moves out of `PLAN.md` each item the batch built or answered, and any item it finds stale: word for word, into `PLAN-history.md`, under the landing's dated heading and the heading the item stood under. The batch's own line in its phase becomes one line, with its landing commit and its review. An open item whose text also stands in another home (a `review-queue.md` entry, a ledger row, a FACTS or POSITIONS entry) becomes one line in `PLAN.md`: what is asked, its default, and a pointer to that home. No other step takes an item out of `PLAN.md`, which held 519K characters before its consolidation of 2026-10-15, 54 % of them closed (`process-engineering/plan-map.md`, sections 2 and 4).
3. FACTS consolidated as its README says, superseded text moved to `FACTS-history.md`. The commit stage has already written the landed count and distance, and the two stages' seconds (F-53, F-240).
4. The skills, in three moves:
   - One task for the standing skill writer (`tools/skill-writer.sh`, its brief `skill-writer-brief.md`): the batch's revival-change material, the section "Revival changes, for the skill writer" of its `RECORD.md`; the skill sentences that the post-batch review lists as false; and any `skill-touched` item. The writer runs `tools/skills-lint.py` before each commit.
   - A cold read of the parts the writer changed, by an agent given only the skill and `skill-cold-read-brief.md`.
   - The writer fixes the cold read's flags, and the coordinator pushes its commits.
5. The next batch launched only after that, so that its workers read the updated skill (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing").
6. The combined post-batch review, started at the landing, since step 4 takes its list of false skill sentences (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing").

The review explains every new or risen row of the checker count by a named rung edit. It reads the microGPT walk check's result. It reports the batch's measures against the batches before it with `tools/batch-measures.py` on the run's directory (`batch-redesign.md`, "The measures").

## An agent that comes back with nothing

<!-- The clarity workflow: rewrite POSITIONS or FACTS entries so that each reads on its own, with a cold read and a fidelity check, as a Workflow run; how to run it and what to do with its output. -->

# The clarity workflow

`record-clarity.js` rewrites record entries so that a reader who knows the language, but never saw the conversation or the batch behind an entry, can tell what it says. It is the process of the clarity pilot of 2026-10-22 (`positions-audit/clarity/`, ten POSITIONS entries, approved and applied at `6b560762f`), run as a Workflow, in the shape of the `fortress-repo` skill rewrite of 2026-10-08 (Workflow run `wf_185878c8-0fb`: writers, cold readers, a fix round). Its standard is Astra's review, `explorations/reviews/revival-record-synthesis.md`.

## What runs, for each chunk of about ten entries

1. **Assess** (FACTS only): Astra's rubric over every entry (`assess.md`); a disposition each: keep, reword, reorganize or investigate. Only reword and reorganize go on.
2. **Write**: the stream's headless Opus writer (`writer-stream.sh`, the skill writer's standing brief) with `writer.md`. For POSITIONS its evidence is the provenance audit's, by `entries.py`; for FACTS, the assessment and each entry's cited sources. A Sonnet step only runs the command and waits (`wait.py`).
3. **Cold read**: an Opus reader with only the `fortress-repo` skill's core and area parts, never its revival part (`coldread.md`).
4. **Check**: fidelity against the sources, and the reader's answers against the source meaning (`check.md`).
5. **Fix**: the writer's second round (`fix.md`), in the same stream, so it resumes the session that wrote the chunk with its evidence in the cache.
6. **Reread**: a second cold read of the fixed entries.
7. **Judge**: once, per entry, apply or hold (`judge.md`), so that no chunk loops; it writes `final.apply` and `queue.md`.

**The writer stream.** One headless Opus session per Workflow run takes its chunks in turn (`flock`), resumed while its context stays under 400K tokens written and its cache is warm (under 50 minutes idle), and started fresh otherwise. In the pilot its fix round wrote 61K tokens, where a fresh writer would read everything again. A Workflow runs at most two agents at once on this machine: run several side by side, each with its own stream.

## Running it

    Workflow({ scriptPath: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/record-clarity.js',
               args: { kind: 'positions' | 'facts', out: '/abs/folder/', stream: 'name', chunks: [{ name: 'c1', entries: ['P-7', 'P-8'] }] } })

`from: 'judge'` runs only the judge, on chunks written before the judge existed.

To correct what a review found, put `findings.md` in each chunk's folder before the run: one block per entry, each finding with the sentence at issue, the right reading and its ground.

Each chunk's files land in `out` + its name: `proposals.md`, `clean.txt`, `proposals.apply`, `concepts.md`, `cold-read.md`, `check.md`, `cold-read-2.md`, `judgement.md`, `final.apply`, `queue.md`, the writer's logs, and for FACTS `assessment.md`. Resume a killed run with the same script path, `resumeFromRunId` and the same args, byte for byte.

## After a chunk

The coordinator's part is mechanical:
- apply the judge's `final.apply` on a copy of the record, `record.py check --base`, then on `main`, and commit the record with the chunk's files;
- file `queue.md` in `review-queue.md` (a worker, for several chunks at once);
- merge `concepts.md` into the concepts list that the orientation workflow reads.

POSITIONS entries need the provenance audit's evidence first: for entries it has not traced, run the mining workflow (`positions-audit/README.md`).
=======
export const meta = {
  name: 'record-clarity',
  description: 'Clarity pass over record entries, POSITIONS or FACTS: per chunk, for FACTS an assessment first, then the stream\'s headless Opus writer, a cold read, a check, the writer\'s fix round, a second cold read and a judge; nothing applied',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Assess', detail: 'FACTS only: the rubric over every entry, a disposition each', model: 'opus' },
    { title: 'Write', detail: 'one writer per chunk, the standing brief and writer.md', model: 'opus' },
    { title: 'ColdRead', detail: 'a reader with only the worker skill', model: 'opus' },
    { title: 'Check', detail: 'fidelity against the sources, and the reader against the meaning', model: 'opus' },
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'the writer\'s second round', model: 'opus' },
    { title: 'Reread', detail: 'a second cold read of the fixed entries', model: 'opus' },
    { title: 'Judge', detail: 'apply or hold each entry, once', model: 'opus' },
  ],
}

// args: { kind: 'positions' | 'facts', out: '/abs/folder/', chunks: [{ name: 'c1', entries: ['P-7', 'P-8'] }],
//         stream: 'name' (the writer stream, default the first chunk's name), from: 'judge' (only judge chunks already written) }
// The writer and its fix round run in the stream's headless Opus session (writer-stream.sh), driven by a
// Sonnet step that only runs the command and waits; the stream resumes its session while the context is small.
// Every agent writes its own files into out + chunk name + '/'. The judge writes final.apply and queue.md;
// the coordinator applies final.apply with record.py, files queue.md and commits. Nothing here touches the record.
const T = '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/'
const KIND = args.kind
const OUT = args.out
const cut = (s, n) => (s ? String(s).slice(0, n) : null)
const ASSESS = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: { rewrite: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } }, summary: { type: 'string' } },
  required: ['rewrite', 'summary'],
}
const STREAM = args.stream || args.chunks[0].name
const FROM = args.from || 'assess'
const drive = (x, n, brief) => {
  const task = `Read your brief and follow it: ${T}${brief}. Your kind: ${KIND}. Your chunk: ${x.name}. Your entries: ${x.write.join(', ')}. Your folder: ${x.dir}`
  const log = `${x.dir}writer-${n}.log`, done = `${x.dir}writer-${n}.done`
  return agent(`You drive a long command and report its output; you judge nothing and write nothing else. The folder ${x.dir} may not exist yet: create it with mkdir -p.
1. If ${done} exists, skip to step 3.
2. Run this in the background with the Bash tool's run_in_background, exactly:
   ${T}writer-stream.sh ${STREAM} "${task}" > ${log} 2>&1; touch ${done}
3. Run \`python3 ${T}wait.py ${done} 540\` in the foreground, with a timeout of 600000 ms. If it exits 1, run it again; repeat until it exits 0.
4. Your final message: the last 60 lines of ${log}, verbatim.`, { label: `${n === 1 ? 'write' : 'fix'} ${x.name}`, phase: n === 1 ? 'Write' : 'Fix', model: 'sonnet' })
}
const tell = (x, extra) => `Your kind: ${KIND}. Your chunk: ${x.name}. Your entries: ${x.write.join(', ')}. Your folder: ${x.dir}` + (extra ? '\n' + extra : '')

const res = await pipeline(args.chunks,
  async (c) => {
    const dir = OUT + c.name + '/'
    if (FROM === 'judge') return { name: c.name, dir, write: c.entries, judgeOnly: true }
    if (KIND !== 'facts') return { name: c.name, dir, write: c.entries }
    const a = await agent(`Read your brief and follow it: ${T}assess.md\n\nYour chunk: ${c.name}. Its entries: ${c.entries.join(', ')}. Your folder: ${dir}`,
      { label: `assess ${c.name}`, phase: 'Assess', model: 'opus', schema: ASSESS })
    return { name: c.name, dir, write: a ? a.rewrite : [], assess: a ? cut(a.summary, 1200) : 'assessment failed' }
  },
  async (x) => {
    if (!x.write.length) return { ...x, skipped: 'nothing to rewrite' }
    if (x.judgeOnly) return x
    const w = await drive(x, 1, 'writer.md')
    return { ...x, writer: cut(w, 1500) }
  },
  async (x) => {
    if (x.skipped || x.judgeOnly) return x
    const r = await agent(`Read your brief and follow it: ${T}coldread.md\n\nThe file to read: ${x.dir}clean.txt\nYour report: ${x.dir}cold-read.md`,
      { label: `cold read ${x.name}`, phase: 'ColdRead', model: 'opus' })
    return { ...x, coldread: cut(r, 1000) }
  },
  async (x) => {
    if (x.skipped || x.judgeOnly) return x
    const r = await agent(`Read your brief and follow it: ${T}check.md\n\n` + tell(x),
      { label: `check ${x.name}`, phase: 'Check', model: 'opus' })
    return { ...x, check: cut(r, 1500) }
  },
  async (x) => {
    if (x.skipped || x.judgeOnly) return x
    const r = await drive(x, 2, 'fix.md')
    return { ...x, fix: cut(r, 1500) }
  },
  async (x) => {
    if (x.skipped || x.judgeOnly) return x
    const r = await agent(`Read your brief and follow it: ${T}coldread.md\n\nThe file to read: ${x.dir}clean.txt\nYour report: ${x.dir}cold-read-2.md`,
      { label: `reread ${x.name}`, phase: 'Reread', model: 'opus' })
    return { ...x, reread: cut(r, 1000) }
  },
  async (x) => {
    if (x.skipped) return x
    const r = await agent(`Read your brief and follow it: ${T}judge.md\n\n` + tell(x),
      { label: `judge ${x.name}`, phase: 'Judge', model: 'opus' })
    return { ...x, judge: cut(r, 1200) }
  },
)
return res

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# writer-stream.sh STREAM TASK...: one task for a stream's headless Opus writer, resumed while its context
# is small and its prompt cache warm, started fresh otherwise.
#
# A stream is one writer that takes its chunks in turn, so that a chunk's fix round resumes the session that
# wrote it and holds its evidence in the cache: the clarity pilot's fix round wrote 61K tokens where a fresh
# writer reads everything again. A headless session keeps its cache for an hour; a Workflow agent's lives five
# minutes. The writer's standing brief is the skill writer's (../../skill-writer-brief.md), with the clarity
# writer's brief (writer.md, or the orientation's); TASK is the rest of the command line, sent as the task.
#
# A fresh session starts when the stream has none, when its context passes LIMIT tokens written (default
# 400K), or when its last task ended more than 50 minutes ago. Tasks of one stream run one at a time (flock).
# The state is under the repository's tmp/record-writer/STREAM/ (ignored): session, written, last, and each
# task's JSON. Prints the writer's report, then one line: session, new or resumed, tokens written.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.." && pwd)
stream=${1:?stream}; shift
task="$*"; [ -n "$task" ] || { echo "usage: $0 STREAM TASK..." >&2; exit 2; }
state="$repo/tmp/record-writer/$stream"; mkdir -p "$state"
LIMIT=${LIMIT:-400000}
tools=(Read Edit Write Glob Grep
       "Bash(python3 -I explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/entries.py:*)"
       "Bash(explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh:*)"
       "Bash(python3 explorations/coordinator/curator-profile/show.py:*)"
       "Bash(git show:*)" "Bash(git log:*)" "Bash(git grep:*)" "Bash(git diff:*)" "Bash(wc:*)" "Bash(ls:*)")
cd "$repo"
exec 9>"$state/lock"; flock 9
now=$(date +%s)
fresh=1
if [ -f "$state/session" ] && [ -f "$state/last" ] && [ -f "$state/written" ]; then
  if [ $(( now - $(cat "$state/last") )) -lt 3000 ] && [ "$(cat "$state/written")" -lt "$LIMIT" ]; then fresh=0; fi
fi
out="$state/$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).json"
if [ $fresh = 1 ]; then
  id=$(python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())'); echo "$id" > "$state/session"; echo 0 > "$state/written"
  { cat explorations/coordinator/skill-writer-brief.md
    printf '\n# This session\n\nYou are a stream writer: the coordinating session sends you tasks one after another, each a chunk of record entries or a part of a skill to write or fix. Your standing order above holds for every task, except its parts on skill files, on committing and on sources.md, which your task brief replaces. Commit nothing.\n\n# Your first task\n\n%s\n' "$task"; } |
    claude -p --model opus --session-id "$id" --permission-mode acceptEdits \
      --allowedTools "${tools[@]}" --output-format json > "$out"
else
  id=$(cat "$state/session")
  printf '# Your next task\n\n%s\n' "$task" |
    claude -p --model opus --resume "$id" --permission-mode acceptEdits \
      --allowedTools "${tools[@]}" --output-format json > "$out"
fi
date +%s > "$state/last"
python3 - "$out" "$state/written" "$fresh" <<'PY'
import json, sys
d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
u = d.get('usage') or {}
w = u.get('cache_creation_input_tokens', 0) + u.get('input_tokens', 0)
total = int(open(sys.argv[2]).read() or 0) + w
open(sys.argv[2], 'w').write(str(total))
print(d.get('result', ''))
print('---')
print('session', d.get('session_id'), 'new' if sys.argv[3] == '1' else 'resumed', 'written', w, 'context', total)
PY
=====
<!-- The clarity workflow's writer brief: rewrite record entries (POSITIONS or FACTS) so that a reader who knows the language but never saw the work behind them understands each one; meaning unchanged. From the clarity pilot of 2026-10-22 (positions-audit/clarity/). -->

You are the writer of the clarity pass in the Fortress revival repository, `/home/user/fortress`. First read your standing brief, `explorations/coordinator/skill-writer-brief.md`, sections 1 to 4, and follow them: the register and the writing principles. Its parts on skill files, on being a resumed session and on committing do not apply here: you write record entries, and you commit nothing.

Your launch message gives your kind (`positions` or `facts`), your entries and your folder. Change no tracked file but the files in your folder.

## The problem

The record is the project's memory, under `explorations/coordinator/`. `POSITIONS.md` holds the curator's decisions; the curator is the person in charge of the project. `FACTS.md` holds what is established about the tree. Their entries are too compressed: they lean on handles, short forms and phrasing that make sense only to someone who was in the conversation or the batch that produced them. Rewrite your entries so that a reader who knows the language, or can look its terms up in the `fortress-repo` skill, can tell without that history:

- for a position: what the curator decided, where it applies and its limits, what it requires a worker to do, and what is unfinished;
- for a fact: what is established and under which conditions (path, library, call form, values), what it means for the work and its limits, and its evidence.

Keep the meaning.

## Read first

- The standard: `explorations/reviews/revival-record-synthesis.md`. For positions, its sections "P45: fidelity and comprehensibility are separate checks" and "For Fable: rewrite positions before consolidating Revival". For facts, "For Claude: assess all FACTS, rewrite only failing entries", its entry schema above all.
- What an entry holds: `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md`, "What an entry is".
- Your entries and their evidence:
  - positions: `python3 -I explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/entries.py N...` prints each entry and the provenance audit's evidence: the scout's report on the curator's messages behind it, with his exact quotes, and the audit's judgement, corrections and takeaway sections. Read the evidence before you write an entry.
  - facts: `assessment.md` in your folder holds the assessor's table and, for each entry you are given, what fails and why. `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'F-N+'` prints an entry with its linked entries, and `'history:F-N'` its history. Read the report section each entry cites before you change a claim.
  - findings: if your folder holds `findings.md`, a review found faults in some of your entries, each with its ground. Correct each sentence that a finding names from its ground, opened at its source: there, and only there, the meaning changes. State the corrected reading as the decision and its reason, and point to the FACTS entry or the report section that holds its ground; the ground's dates, counts, commits and file names go in the apply file's note line, not in the entry. Change nothing that no finding names, and let an entry grow only by what its corrections need. Where a finding's only ground is a reviewer's reasoning, or it needs the curator's word, keep the text and write a question for the curator.

## How to write each entry

1. The bold title states the decision or the fact in plain words, no broader than the body.
2. Then its scope and its exact conditions. Keep every condition, exception and limit. A shorter sentence must not lose one.
3. For a position, the reason after "Why:", only if the curator gave one or accepted it in the question, or a finding in `findings.md` gives it with its ground in the team's texts, library or code. For a fact, its evidence: the test, measurement, source reading or report section, and whether it was observed, read in the code or inferred.
4. Keep the state apart: "Built.", or "Still to build:" in one line with where the work is tracked. Keep such lines as they are; do not move them out.
5. Name each thing. Say which call, which checker, which library, which path, when a sentence has two of them. Use no handle of a past conversation or batch ("answer 9", "ask 3", "item 48", "rung C", "decision E") unless a skill defines it.
6. **Pointers.** For each pointer (another entry, a gap-ledger row, a PLAN item, a report), decide first whether it belongs in the entry. If it stays, give it a few words on what it holds, so that a reader can decide whether to follow it without loading it. If it is only provenance, move it to the apply file's note line, where a bare reference is fine.
7. **Concepts.** Define a concept in the entry only if it belongs to this entry alone. List any other concept that a reader needs in `concepts.md` in your folder: the term, the entries that use it, and where it should be defined for every worker (the `fortress-repo` core, an area part, or the short orientation that will replace the revival part). The revival part is being rewritten: do not lean on it.
8. Do not add a claim, a reason or a scope that the sources do not hold. Do not make a claim stronger or broader. Where the sources leave the meaning open, keep the current wording for that part and write a question for the curator.
9. For a fact: keep a historical measurement only if it is stated as that measurement; move repair chronology to the history; link a count that changes at every landing to the entry that owns it. A fact may record an implementation choice made at a default; say so, and never as the curator's ruling.
10. Keep each entry near 600 characters as a check, not a cap. Clarity comes first.

## Your files, in your folder

- `proposals.md`, with a header comment of one sentence. For each entry: the clean entry first, as the record would hold it; then "Meaning: unchanged", or each change of meaning you could not avoid, with its source; then the source of each sentence; then any question for the curator.
- `clean.txt`: the clean entries only, one per line. A cold reader gets this file alone.
- `proposals.apply`: each entry's line, then one indented line `  by: the clarity pass; note: WHY`, with the provenance pointers that left the entry. The coordinator applies it with `record.py`.
- `concepts.md`, as in step 7.

Your final message: the files' paths, and one line per entry on what made it hard to read and what you did.
=====
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""wait.py FILE [SECONDS]: wait until FILE exists, at most SECONDS (default 540); print it if it does.

A Workflow agent that drives a long command runs it in the background, writing FILE when it ends, and calls
this until it prints. Exit 0 when FILE exists, 1 on timeout."""
import os, sys, time
f, limit = sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 540
end = time.time() + limit
while time.time() < end:
    if os.path.exists(f):
        print(open(f).read()); sys.exit(0)
    time.sleep(10)
sys.exit(1)

===== assess.md
<!-- The clarity workflow's assessment brief, for FACTS: Astra's rubric over every entry of a chunk, a disposition for each, before any rewrite. -->

You are an Opus assessor in the Fortress revival repository (`/home/user/fortress`). Change nothing but your own report file. Commit nothing.

`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md` holds what the project has established about the tree, one numbered entry each. Your launch message gives your entries and your folder. Assess each entry by the rubric of `explorations/reviews/revival-record-synthesis.md`, section "For Claude: assess all FACTS, rewrite only failing entries": read that section first, its entry schema and its rubric above all, and `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md`, "What an entry is".

For each entry: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'F-N+'` prints it with its linked entries, and `'history:F-N'` its history. Follow its cited evidence as far as the retained claim needs: the report section, the test, the code. Read bounded sections; rerun no experiment and search no transcript; where either would be needed, record the narrow gap.

Mark each criterion pass, fail or unresolved, with a short reason, and a quoted passage for each fail: scope, present meaning, evidence, comprehension, ownership, consistency. Do not average them. Then give each entry one disposition:

- **keep:** every criterion passes;
- **reword:** the meaning is sound and supported, but its wording or the wording of its scope fails;
- **reorganize:** detail to move, a merge with an entry that owns the subject, or a split of claims that change apart;
- **investigate:** support or consistency is unresolved; state the narrow question that would settle it.

Do not mark an entry for a rewrite to make its surface like the others. Age is not a criterion.

Write `assessment.md` in your folder: one row per entry, its six marks with their reasons, its disposition, and for each fail the quoted passage. Your structured result: the entries to rewrite (those marked reword or reorganize), and a summary with the counts by disposition and the investigate questions.
===== coldread.md
<!-- The clarity workflow's cold-read brief: read the rewritten entries with only the worker's skill, and say what each one means. -->

You are a cold reader in the Fortress revival repository (`/home/user/fortress`). def entries(text):
    return {m.group(1): l[2:] for l in text.split('\n') for m in [re.match(r'- (P-\d+) ', l)] if m}

def where(path, n):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""words-subset.py APPLY [--allow WORD ...]: check that a scrape only deletes.

For each entry line `- F-87 ...` or `- P-48 ...` of the apply file, compare its
words with the entry as FACTS.md or POSITIONS.md holds it now: every word of the
new line must occur in the old one at least as often (case and punctuation
ignored), so that words can be deleted or reordered but none added. --allow
names words that may be added (default: none). Prints each entry that adds a
word, with the words added, and exits 1 if there is any; new entries (`F-?1`)
are reported as not allowed.
"""
import re, sys
from collections import Counter

ROOT = '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/'
args = sys.argv[1:]
allow = set()
if '--allow' in args:
    i = args.index('--allow'); allow = {w.lower() for w in args[i + 1:]}; args = args[:i]
words = lambda s: Counter(w.lower() for w in re.findall(r"[\w'`\\-]+", s))
old = {}
for f in ('FACTS.md', 'POSITIONS.md'):
    for l in open(ROOT + f):
        m = re.match(r'- ([FP]-\d+) ', l)
        if m: old[m.group(1)] = l
bad = 0; n = 0
for l in open(args[0]):
    m = re.match(r'- ([FP]-[\d?]+) ', l)
    if not m: continue
    n += 1; k = m.group(1)
    if k not in old: print(f'{k}: not an existing entry'); bad += 1; continue
    added = words(l) - words(old[k])
    added = {w: c for w, c in added.items() if w not in allow}
    if added: bad += 1; print(f'{k}: adds ' + ', '.join(f'{w}' + (f' x{c}' if c > 1 else '') for w, c in added.items()))
print(f'words-subset: {n} entries, {bad} add words')
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

<!-- The account of why the POSITIONS rewrite of 2026-10-26 failed where the consolidation of 2026-10-21 to 22 succeeded, and of how to run the foundations review's corrections now, written on 2026-10-28 by an Opus worker from the map and the evidence files beside it, and revised on 2026-10-28 after the curator's recheck, with its pronouns named, for the coordinator and the curator. -->

# Why the POSITIONS rewrite of 10-26 failed, and how to run the corrections

Times are UTC. From 10-25 the curator's time is UTC+1. Paths start at `explorations/` unless they start at `.claude/`. Five evidence files are cited by short names:

- "timeline": `coordinator/postmortem-2026-10-28/evidence/timeline-10-26-to-10-28.md`, by the time of a message;
- "recheck": `.../evidence/scope-recheck.md`, by section;
- "genesis": `.../evidence/brief-genesis.md`, by section, with the run brief's instructions I1 to I29;
- "consolidation": `.../evidence/last-consolidation.md`, by section;
- "history": `.../evidence/tools-and-skills-history.md`, by section.

"My count" marks a figure that this account measured itself.

## Summary for the coordinator

**The causes, heaviest first.** The steps up to the launch were right (section 1).

1. The coordinator asked the Fable judge for a list of behaviours, then made it binding over the clarity tool's guard. The run brief said "Each rewritten entry must produce every behaviour listed for it" and "Where they differ, this brief wins", through the coordinator's hook. The list carried batch numbers, counts and dates; the coordinator added "the year of each ground". The texts grew to 1.9 times the entries and carried history: the curator's complaints of length and "historical events".
2. A fresh boot wrote the brief eight minutes after a compaction, at 466K. Its plan came from the boot note and its content from the judgement, unchecked against `record.md`. It gives no length cap and no register.
3. The skills name no tool for correcting entries after a review. No rule says that a run gives a tool data, not rules. The lessons that would have stopped it stayed in a tool brief, a README, a commit message and the held list.
4. Nothing caught it before the end: no pilot, no length cap, and a trap test that checks decisions only. It scored 12 of 12 on the rejected texts.
5. After the rejection, four framings in two days. The last was an ask the curator could not read.

**Did the skill changes after the consolidation encode the practice wrongly or too thinly? Too thinly.** The 14 commits of 10-22 and 10-23 to the coordinator skill and `fortress-repo`'s records part are right, but they name what each tool does, not the job it fits: no tool for corrections, no rule 0, no pilot. One cut the only mention of the clarity tool's fidelity check. Only the coordinator's hook changed the tool; the model stayed Opus.

**How to run the corrections.**

- Scope: the 18 entries with findings in `explorations/reviews/foundations/evidence/salvage-findings.md`, every finding.
- Tool: the clarity workflow, kind `positions`, with one change to its own briefs (proposal 0). With `findings.md` in a chunk's folder, the writer corrects each finding by the audit's rules, rule 0 ("change as little as you can") first, and changes nothing else. The checker fails any other change, and any growth beyond need. No run brief.
- Two chunks of nine, by subject. The first runs alone. An Opus page writer shows the curator its texts, old beside new. Then the second.
- Checks: the tool's cold reads, check, fix and judge; `record.py check --base`, a length table and `words-subset.py` on a copy; the trap test of 10-26 again, blind, about 0.8M.
- The coordinator now writes no entry text, edits no judged file, and only copies files, launches, applies with `record.py` at the curator's yes, and commits. About 2.5M to 3.5M tokens written in all, an estimate.

**Decisions for the curator** (section 7): the brief change, or the mining workflow instead; the pilot; whether five findings awaiting the curator's word go into the run as questions; the quiz; three skill proposals.

## 1. What happened, 10-26 to 10-28

All from the timeline unless marked.

- **10-26 07:37 to 08:38: the steps up to the launch** (recheck). The coordinator put two changes to POSITIONS: "Three more wait for the Fable judgement." (07:38:21). The curator approved the two, one library (P-37) and the team's later word (P-26), with the clarity workflow and a trap test: a test of whether a reader acting as the coordinator decides right from the new text where the old text leads wrong (07:42:15). The coordinator stated the extension: "They also cover every other entry that the judgement says bends or lacks its real reason." (07:49:25). The curator assented: "Yeah, this sounds like a solid plan." (07:54:36). The Fable judge was asked "Which entries bend" (08:10:52), and named 12. The compaction carried the rewrites as "already approved" (08:29:38). Each of these steps was right. At 08:37 to 08:38 the coordinator wrote a run brief of 7.7K for 13 entries, hooked it into four stages of the clarity tool (`bedc80b01`), and launched the run.
- **09:26 to 12:13.** Both judges applied all 13 texts; the coordinator edited five. The trap test scored them 12 of 12, the old entries 10 of 12. A page put them to the curator (`reviews/foundations/rewrite-results.md`).
- **19:08 to 19:26.** The curator rejected them, and called the coordinator's proposal to keep two sentences weaseling. The cost was about 2.7M tokens written, against 1.5M estimated.
- **10-27 07:12 to 07:47.** The curator asked to salvage small, targeted corrections, and ruled that Fable writes no text that enters the record as written (`coordinator/HELD.md`, "Held in chat (2026-10-27)"), and refused the coordinator's new plan, which reinvented workflows that exist.
- **22:14 to 23:35.** The hook was undone (`18788035c`). The coordinator said it should write the corrections itself. A Sonnet worker's findings list came in: 40 entries named, 18 with findings.
- **10-28 05:40 to 05:56.** On Opus, the coordinator put a scope ask in the numbers of its own sort. The curator could not read it, and switched the coordinator to Fable.
- **07:37 and 07:42.** The curator ruled for the clarity workflow, chunked, an Opus writer, never the coordinator's hand, over every finding; and asked for this account (`coordinator/HELD.md`, "Held in chat (2026-10-28)").

## 2. What went wrong, and why

### The causes, heaviest first

The causes are what bent the run brief, and what let its texts through.

**1. The run brief made the Fable judgement's list binding, over the tool's guard.** The coordinator's reasoning. The curator had asked for this tool so that the proven process, with its cold reader, would write the entries, not the coordinator with its full context: "you can use for writing it with a code reader" (07:42:15; "code" is "cold", dictated).

- The list was the coordinator's design: its judge brief asked, "For each entry to rewrite", what the new text must make the coordinator do (07:58:56), and the compaction summary carried the plan "per judgement section 7" (genesis §3).
- The run brief set aside the clarity writer's "Keep the meaning." (I4) and made the list binding: "Each rewritten entry must produce every behaviour listed for it" (I5); "A behaviour of section 7 that the text does not produce is a failure" (I27). It reached four stages and said "Where they differ, this brief wins." (I2). The override and its hook (`bedc80b01`) have no source but the coordinator (genesis).
- Section 7 gives up to six behaviours an entry, with batch numbers, counts and dates: "closed by 22c", "is 52 walls now", "his 09-20 class-loader lean". The coordinator added "give the year of each ground it ranks" (I17, no source found).
- My count: the 13 texts hold 21.2K characters against 11.2K in the entries, 1.9 times. The team's later word (P-26) grew from 1.2K to 3.2K, one library (P-37) from 1.1K to 2.9K (`reviews/foundations/evidence/rewrite/combined.apply` against `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`). The years it asked for fit the curator's "historical events".
- The writer was Opus (`reviews/foundations/evidence/salvage-inventory.md`, piece 3). Its first source and target was the 55K Fable judgement. That this carried Fable's register in is my inference; nothing measured it.

**2. A fresh boot wrote the brief from the plan, without the record's rules.** The coordinator's situation (genesis).

- An automatic compaction came at 08:29:38, at 796K. The brief came eight minutes later, at 466K: 124K after the compaction, 17K of skills, 235K of boot reading and 90K of work.
- In the coordinator's words (19:22:55, 19:27:02): "Its plan came from the boot note." and "The fresh session carried the plan out without checking it against `record.md`." Its content came from the judgement and the dialogue.
- The brief names none of the record's rules for an entry: near 600 characters, one or two sentences, ASD-STE100. "keep each entry as short as the behaviours allow" (I7) gives no number.
- At 08:36:59 it planned "a small change so the clarity workflow can carry this run's extra brief, then the brief itself". The hook, the brief, the commit and the launch took 65 seconds.

**3. The tool did not fit the job, and the skills did not say so.** The skills' text and the tools' limits.

- The skill gives the clarity workflow one job: "Run it when entries no longer read on their own." (`.claude/skills/coordinator/references/record.md`, "The consolidation tools"). No tool is named for correcting what a review found.
- On 10-21 to 22 the audit's writer made the content corrections, by rule 0 and its other rules (`coordinator/positions-audit/full/evidence/briefs/writer.md`, "The rules").
- The clarity tool has no input for findings (`record-clarity.js`). The coordinator saw the conflict (I4), and changed the tool without the curator's word: `bedc80b01` cites none (history §2). The skill asks it to propose a fix (rules below).

**4. Nothing caught it before the end.** The coordinator's choices and the tools' limits.

- No pilot: the curator saw all 13 texts at once, after the test.
- No length cap and no length check (`coordinator/BOOT.md`, "Waiting on him").
- The trap test checks decisions only. It passed 12 of 12 (`rewrite-results.md`, "The trap test"). No tool checks register, length against the version before, or history in an entry (my reading of the tool's briefs).
- Both judges held nothing; on 10-22 they held 6 of 65 (consolidation §1, step 13).

**5. After the rejection, four framings.** The coordinator's choices (timeline).

- Keep two sentences (10-26 19:11:14). A new process (10-27 07:31, refused). Write the corrections by its own hand (22:56:47), from "The pass owns each entry's final wording" (`record.md`). An ask in its sort's numbers, "a. Write 1 to 10, and do 11" (10-28 05:40:11), refused as undecipherable.

### The rules the coordinator broke

All but one stood before the consolidation that worked (my check by `git blame` and `git log -S`):

- "If its words would defeat its purpose, do the better thing, say so in one line, and propose a fix." (`SKILL.md`, "The curator's role and decisions").
- "The problem, never the expected answer." and "For an update of a document: a length cap against the version before." (`references/delegating.md`, "What a brief holds", `f6bc1aa75`).
- "An entry states the present, or what holds for all time." (`record.md`, "What an entry is", `ef6a0a026`, 10-22, a lesson of the consolidation). Question 3 there, a date goes "to the history" (`7b434aae5`), and "Keep an entry near 600 characters." (`cb9213556`, 10-14).
- "Use no internal shorthand." (`SKILL.md`, "Talking to the curator"): the ask of 10-28 05:40:11.

### The failures that no rule covered

- A run brief that overrides a tool's own briefs.
- Which tool corrects entries after a review.
- A pilot that the curator reads before a run rewrites many entries.
- A check of length, register and history. The tools check meaning and decisions only.
- Two homes for writing entries: "The pass" and "A consolidation" (`record.md`). The skill does not say which one governs a correction of 18 entries. The coordinator chose the first at 22:56:47 on 10-27; the curator ruled for the second at 07:37 on 10-28.

### What the evidence does not show

A full context does not separate the windows: on 10-22 the clarity runs launched at 489K to 708K, and succeeded (consolidation §1). On both days the coordinator's own writing failed: on 10-22 its explanation and 24 proposals, "horribly vaguely written" (consolidation §3, 16:28:00); on 10-26 the run brief. On 10-22 that writing stayed out of the tools; on 10-26 the hook put it in.

## 3. The last consolidation, its lessons, and where they went

### What it did right that 10-26 did not

1. **Each tool ran on its own briefs.** A launch message held two lines: the brief's path, then the entries and the folder (consolidation §2). The curator shaped the audit's briefs by page comments and gave rule 0 (history §5, `317f24091`).
2. **The tool fit the job.** The audit's writer made the content corrections by rule 0. The clarity writer then kept their meaning (consolidation §1, steps 4 to 13).
3. **A pilot came first, and the curator read it**: ten entries in the audit's trial, ten in the clarity pilot, then "I felt the tone was good." (consolidation §3, 08:19:30).
4. **The writers wrote from the curator's words**: 1,100 quotes, all checked exact (`coordinator/positions-audit/full/RESULTS.md`, "The checks"). On 10-26 the first source was the Fable judgement.
5. **The coordinator's part was mechanical**: apply, check, commit (`coordinator/tools/record-clarity/README.md`, "After a chunk"). On 10-26 it wrote the run brief and edited five judged texts (`combined.apply`, header).
6. **The judges held what they doubted**, with the old text as the default (consolidation §1, step 13; §4, item 9).

### Which lessons reached the skills and tools

Reached: section 4 gives each commit.

Not reached:

- Rule 0: only in the audit's writer brief. The merge of the two writers: only in the audit's README. No run brief overrides a tool's briefs: only in the message of `18788035c`. A pilot that the curator reads first: nowhere.
- A change of this size by tools, never by the coordinator's hand: on the held list (10-28 07:37).
- The record-test kit: no tool's README names it (history §6, "Not found").
- The recipe of 10-13 in `record.md`, "A consolidation" (chunks of 20 to 32, a scout, a writer, a quiz) still stands beside the tools section. The runs of 10-22 followed the tools, and no quiz ran on POSITIONS (consolidation §0).

## 4. Did a change to the skills or tools degrade the coordinator?

content.content:
## 4. Did a change to the skills or tools degrade the coordinator?

Not by wrong text, but by thin text. From 10-22 09:32 to the launch, 14 commits changed the coordinator skill or `fortress-repo`'s records part, the last at 10-23 19:16 (history §6; my reading of the diffs).

- `b6f5268e1` (10-22 09:32): entries that read on their own, the six checks, "The consolidation tools" with the mining workflow first, every writer on Opus, writer streams, one judge a round. Right, but thin (cause 3). The mining workflow only "finds where each POSITIONS entry came from": that its writer corrected by rule 0 is left out. So is what would have stopped 10-26: section 3's "Not reached".
- `ef6a0a026` (12:22): "An entry states the present, or what holds for all time." Right; the 10-26 texts broke it.
- `6becc28f9` (14:26), wording fixes. It cut the clarity bullet's one mention of the tool's fidelity check. Right, and thinner.
- Right, and of no bearing on entries: `caaf4f13f` (a decision may point to a fact), `c24fcf50a` (evidence folders), `a898e1baf` (terms moved, then back), `617b0d94c`, `0cbb4f5c9`, `3c8ee2acc` (load order, light boot), `404599414` (model check), `d70d78445` and its reversal `5427e7208`; in the records part, ledger commands (`ef6a0a026`, `6becc28f9`, `f6f7de70c`, `2d5820c89`).

The rest held: the rules broken on 10-26 (section 2), the consolidation's own rules (`salvage-inventory.md`, piece 3), the tool but for the hook (history §1, §2), and the model.

## 5. How to run the corrections now

### The job and its scope

- Content corrections to the 18 entries that carry findings in `reviews/foundations/evidence/salvage-findings.md`, every finding in it. The 22 entries named with nothing wrong stay out.
- Not in this run: the review's findings outside POSITIONS (`rewrite-results.md`, "Still owed", last bullet). They go their own way afterwards.
- Not sources: the 13 rejected texts, the run brief, the pages of 10-26. The judgement serves only where a finding cites it, for content, never for wording.

### The tool, and the one change it needs

The clarity workflow, kind `positions`, all its stages, with writer streams. As it stands, its writer cannot see the findings, and its checker would fail every correction as a change of meaning. The smallest change is to its own briefs, written once and reviewed by the curator, so that no run carries rules.

**Proposal 0, for the curator's yes.** Add to `coordinator/tools/record-clarity/writer.md`, after "Keep the meaning.":

> **Corrections.** If your folder holds `findings.md`, a review found faults in some of your entries, each with its ground. For each fault, correct the sentence from its ground, move it to the history, or keep it and write a question for the curator, by the rules of the audit's writer brief, rule 0 first (`explorations/coordinator/positions-audit/full/evidence/briefs/writer.md`, "The rules"). Change nothing that no fault names. An entry grows only by what its corrections need.

Add to `check.md`, under step 1:

> If your folder holds `findings.md`: a change that a fault and its ground support is not a fidelity failure. A change that no fault asks for is one. So is growth beyond what the corrections need, and a sentence that tells how a decision came about.

Add to `README.md`, "Running it": "To correct what a review found, copy its findings into each chunk's folder as `findings.md` before the run." `fix.md` and `judge.md` need nothing. The skill writer, on Opus, makes the edit.

### The steps

1. **Chunk by subject**, two chunks of nine, so that entries that share a rule share a writer:
   - first, the team's word and the one library: the specification's revision (P-7), the team's later word (P-26), the library's practice (P-27), one library (P-37), the flat number types (P-43), the self-type idiom (P-146), the integer power (P-153), list order (P-154), abstract members in an exporting component (P-158);
   - second, the bound, the phases, arrays and native calls: walk runs the checker (P-12), unboxed doubles (P-17), the phase order (P-33), the bound `Any` (P-42), native bindings (P-58), walk's coercions (P-59), the `double[]` store (P-84), the open array questions (P-85), symbolic operators (P-155).
2. **The untraced entry.** The audit never traced abstract members (P-158). The README asks for the mining workflow first, but `entries.py` reads only the audit's fixed chunks, so its trail would not reach the writer. The writer uses P-158's history and the findings' grounds. Say so in one line at the launch.
3. **Copy the data**: `salvage-findings.md` into each chunk's folder as `findings.md`.
4. **Run the first chunk alone**, as the pilot. Keep the arguments byte for byte, for a resume:
   `Workflow({ scriptPath: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/record-clarity.js', args: { kind: 'positions', out: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/consolidation-2026-10-28/evidence/positions/', stream: 'corrections', chunks: [{ name: 'c1', entries: ['P-7', 'P-26', 'P-27', 'P-37', 'P-43', 'P-146', 'P-153', 'P-154', 'P-158'] }] } })`
5. **Mechanical checks**, by a worker on a copy of the record: apply the judge's `final.apply`; `record.py check --base`; each entry's length before and after; `words-subset.py` on the entries whose findings are strikes only.
6. **The curator's read.** An Opus page writer shows the curator the judged texts: the clean entry first, the old one under it, each change with its finding. That read, on tone and length, decides whether the second chunk runs. A change the curator asks for in one entry goes into `findings.md` as a new finding, with the ask's time as its ground, and that entry runs again. A change for every entry goes into the tool's brief, at the curator's yes.
7. **Run the second chunk** the same way, as chunk `c2` with stream `corrections-2` (one stream per run, `delegating.md`), then steps 5 and 6 again.
8. **The quiz**: the trap test of 10-26 again (`reviews/foundations/evidence/trap-test/questions.md`, `key.md`), by the record-test kit (`coordinator/process-engineering/record-test/README.md`). Two detached worktrees, one with the old entries and one with the corrected ones. Remove the foundations review, the conversation note, the kit, this account's folder and the run's folder. One Opus reader in each acts as the coordinating session; one blind Opus grader, as on 10-26 (the kit names Fable), is told the key's slips (`rewrite-results.md`). Pass: no scenario scores lower than with the old entries (10 of 12). About 0.8M tokens written (timeline 09:29 to 09:48).
9. **Apply** at the curator's yes on each text: `record.py apply` on `main` with the judges' files, `check --base`, commit, push. A worker files the judges' `queue.md` items in the review queue.

### The coordinator's part, on Fable

- Copy files, launch, read the judges' final messages and the checks' one-line results, apply with `record.py`, commit.
- Write no entry text, no apply line and no note line. Edit no judged file. Write no run brief: the arguments above are the whole input.
- Cost, an estimate: 1.5M to 2.5M tokens written for the chunks (the 10-26 run wrote 1.62M for 13 entries), 0.8M for the quiz, 0.2M for the page.

## 6. Proposed text for the skills

Each is a proposal for the curator's yes. The skill writer, on Opus, writes it.

**Proposal 1.** `record.md`, "The consolidation tools", the clarity bullet. It replaces "Run it when entries no longer read on their own." with:

> Run it when entries no longer read on their own, and, with a review's findings in each chunk's folder, to correct what the review found (its README).

It adds a tool for the job that had none.

**Proposal 2.** `record.md`, "The consolidation tools", a new last line:

> Give a tool's run its arguments and its data, never rules of your own. If a tool's briefs do not fit the job, say so, and propose the change to the curator.

It adds the rule of `18788035c`, which today lives only in a commit message.

**Proposal 3.** `record.md`, "A consolidation". It replaces the six bullets, the recipe of 10-13, and keeps the line on FACTS before a batch:

> A consolidation, or a correction of more than a few entries, runs as runs of the consolidation tools. You write and edit no entry text in it.
> - Chunk by subject, about ten entries a chunk.
> - Run one chunk first, and show its texts to the curator, old beside new, before the others run.
> - Apply each judge's file with `record.py`, run `check --base`, commit and push.
> - Then test the changed entries with the record-test kit (`process-engineering/record-test/`): the decisions must stay as good.

It settles which part governs: "The pass" for one worker's findings, this part for many entries. It is shorter than the text it replaces.

## 7. Decisions for the curator

None of these is taken.

1. **The tool for the corrections.**
   - a. The clarity workflow, with proposal 0 in its own briefs. Default.
   - b. The mining workflow, its briefs copied to a new folder, with the findings in place of the scouts' reports and the judgement. The clarity tool stays as it is, but there is no fix round and no judge.
   - c. The clarity workflow with a `findings` argument in its script, in place of the file in the folder. It changes the script that the curator had restored at 22:13 on 10-27.
2. **The pilot.**
   - a. The first chunk alone, read by the curator; then the second runs. Default.
   - b. Both chunks in one run, all 18 read by the curator at the end. Faster, and the shape of 10-26.
3. **The findings that read the curator's decisions anew**: the self-type idiom (P-146), the integer power (P-153), list order (P-154); and the yeses the curator still owes on native bindings (P-58) and symbolic operators (P-155).
   - a. In the run: the writer writes a question and no text, and the judge files it in the review queue. Default.
   - b. Out of the run: each is its own ask later, as the coordinator's sort of 10-28 05:38 had it (`reviews/foundations/evidence/salvage-sort.md`).
4. **The quiz.**
   - a. The trap test again, blind, about 0.8M. Default.
   - b. No quiz: the tool's checks and the curator's read only.
5. **Proposals 1 to 3 for the skills**, each yes or no. Default: yes to each, with the skill writer's wording shown to the curator on a page before it lands.

## 8. The quotes that the decisions rest on

- **The curator's go**, 10-26 07:42:15 (timeline): "Yes, to both rewording of or refinements of P37 and P26. But we have like a clarity process workflow that you can use for writing it with a code reader."
- **The run brief** (`reviews/foundations/evidence/rewrite/run-brief.md`): "Where they differ, this brief wins."
- **The clarity writer's guard** (`coordinator/tools/record-clarity/writer.md`): "Keep the meaning." and rule 8: "Do not add a claim, a reason or a scope that the sources do not hold. Do not make a claim stronger or broader."
- **The audit writer's rule 0** (`coordinator/positions-audit/full/evidence/briefs/writer.md`, "The rules"): "Change as little as you can." and "Change only what is factually wrong, not his, or stale".
- **The merge never built** (`coordinator/positions-audit/README.md`, "The mining workflow"): "the correction by the audit's rules and the rewrite for clarity can be one writer stage when the mining runs again."
- **The curator's rejection**, 10-26 19:08:27 (timeline): "It is in the Claude speak. It is not in the ASD-STE100 register. It is not written as a timeless position. It cites things not as principles, but as historical events, things that will go out of date as soon as we make a move in the repo." and "It expands several times over the allotted position length." and "What is the impetus for rewriting this?"
- **The curator's salvage goal**, 10-27 07:12:48 (timeline): "But if there are really other 13 points that need a small targeted corrections, then we should not waste that scout's work or the Opus analysis we did."
- **The curator's refusal of a new process**, 10-27 07:47:43 (timeline): "No. No go. The plan seems to reinvent something for which we already have workflows."
- **The tool restored**, 10-27 22:13:20 (timeline): "Does this mean restoring it to original form that worked well for what it was designed? Yes please, undo the damage." The commit `18788035c`: "no run brief (args.extra) can override its own briefs".
- **The pilot of 10-22**, 08:19:30 (consolidation §3): "I felt the tone was good."
- **The curator's verdict**, 10-28 07:37:43 (consolidation §3): "We already invented this process. We perfected it. It worked well during the last record consolidation. We have probably failed to encode how to use it correctly next time."
- **The curator's rule of 10-28 07:37**, in the coordinator's words on the held list (`coordinator/HELD.md`, "Held in chat (2026-10-28)"): "A batch of entry changes of this size runs through the clarity workflow, chunked, with a specialist Opus writer, never by the coordinator's hand. The scope of the salvage is every issue the review found, not the two changes agreed before".
- **The curator's rule of 10-28 07:26**, the same list, in the coordinator's words: "The skills stay light: no series of rules and cases, which confuse a full context."

## How to read this

- Times are UTC; yours is UTC+1. A time with seconds, such as 13:00:30, is a message in the session transcript. `explorations/coordinator/curator-profile/show.py` prints any message of yours by its time.

- POSITIONS holds your decisions, one entry each, such as P-37. FACTS holds what is established about the tree, such as F-293. Each has a history file that keeps every earlier text of an entry and why it changed.
- "The coordinator" is the coordinating session. A worker is an agent that it launches. Sonnet, Opus and Fable are model tiers. A compaction replaces the session's context with a summary; a boot is the session's start-up reading after one. A page is a web page that the coordinator publishes for you to read and comment on.
- A sentence that starts "My reading:" is my own judgement. Every other sentence states what a cited source says.

## In short

- **What failed.** On 26 October a run of the clarity workflow rewrote 13 POSITIONS entries, and you rejected every text. The clarity workflow is the tool that rewrites record entries so that each reads on its own and keeps its meaning.
- **Why.** The steps up to the run were right. The brief that the coordinator wrote for the run made a worker's list binding over the tool's own rules. The deeper cause, found on 29 October: a worker's report was taken as the plan, with no judgement between report and action.
- **What was done.** The tool was restored and given a findings input at your yes. The corrections ran as a pilot of four entries and two chunks (groups of entries) of seven. Your reading found the next fault: every finding had gone into the entry's text. The findings were sorted by home and by weight, one Opus writer wrote the changes from your comments, and they landed at 13:02 on 29 October.
- **What it taught.** A small pilot that you read was the only check of form that worked. Each finding has a home, and the entry's text is only one. A review that reports every fault needs a sort by significance before anything is written.
- **What is open.** Part 2 of the salvage, three answers of the evening not yet in the record, the skill changes on their branch, and some upkeep (section 7).

<!-- The ledger clarity workflow: bring open gap-ledger rows to the present, as a Workflow run of a writer, a checker and a judge per chunk; how to run it and what to do with its output. -->

# The ledger clarity workflow

`ledger-clarity.js` rewrites open rows of `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md` so that each states its gap as it stands now: a claim that names no fixed half, a reproducer that reproduces it, notes without a repair story. It follows the health check of 2026-10-22 (`explorations/coordinator/ledger-health-2026-10-22/REPORT.md`, sections 5.5 and 6.1), whose rubric is the record's (`explorations/reviews/revival-record-synthesis.md`). It writes nothing to the ledger.

For each chunk of about twelve rows: an Opus writer assesses each row and writes its new line, a close, or an investigate question (`writer.md`); an Opus checker verifies them against the tree (`check.md`); a judge applies or holds each, once (`judge.md`).

    Workflow({ scriptPath: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger-clarity/ledger-clarity.js',
               args: { out: '/abs/folder/', chunks: [{ name: 'l1', rows: ['8', '20'] }] } })

After a chunk: for each line of `final.rewrite`, `ledger.py rewrite N FILE` (one line per file); for each line of `final.closes`, `ledger.py close`; then `ledger.py check` and `ledger.py landing-check BASE`; commit the ledger, its history and the chunk's files; file `queue.md` in `review-queue.md`. Resume a killed run with the same script path, `resumeFromRunId` and the same args.
===== ledger-clarity.js
export const meta = {
  name: 'ledger-clarity',
  description: 'Bring open gap-ledger rows to the present, per chunk: an Opus writer assesses each row by the record rubric and writes its new line or close, a checker verifies them against the tree, a judge applies or holds each once; nothing written to the ledger',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Write', detail: 'assess each row, write its new line, close or question', model: 'opus' },
    { title: 'Check', detail: 'fidelity against the tree, the commits and the tests', model: 'opus' },
    { title: 'Judge', detail: 'apply or hold each row, once', model: 'opus' },
  ],
}

// args: { out: '/abs/folder/', chunks: [{ name: 'l1', rows: ['8', '20'] }] }
// Each chunk's files land in out + name + '/'. The coordinator applies final.rewrite with ledger.py rewrite and
// final.closes with ledger.py close, runs ledger.py check and landing-check, files queue.md and commits.
const T = '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger-clarity/'
const cut = (s, n) => (s ? String(s).slice(0, n) : null)
const tell = (x) => `Your chunk: ${x.name}. Its rows: ${x.rows.join(', ')}. Your folder: ${x.dir} (create it with mkdir -p if it does not exist).`

return await pipeline(args.chunks.map(c => ({ ...c, dir: args.out + c.name + '/' })),
  async (x) => ({ ...x, writer: cut(await agent(`Read your brief and follow it: ${T}writer.md\n\n` + tell(x), { label: `write ${x.name}`, phase: 'Write', model: 'opus' }), 1200) }),
  async (x) => ({ ...x, check: cut(await agent(`Read your brief and follow it: ${T}check.md\n\n` + tell(x), { label: `check ${x.name}`, phase: 'Check', model: 'opus' }), 1000) }),
  async (x) => ({ ...x, judge: cut(await agent(`Read your brief and follow it: ${T}judge.md\n\n` + tell(x), { label: `judge ${x.name}`, phase: 'Judge', model: 'opus' }), 1000) }),
)

===== apply.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""apply.py CHUNK_DIR... [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]: apply judged chunks of the ledger clarity workflow.

For each chunk folder: each line of final.rewrite goes through `ledger.py rewrite N FILE`
(the row's number taken from its first cell), and each line of final.closes
(`N<TAB>HASH<TAB>TEST<TAB>NOTE`) through `ledger.py close`. --root, --ledger and --history pass through to
ledger.py, so a run on copies of the ledger and its history writes nothing real. Stops at the first
refusal and prints it.
"""
import re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, os
args = sys.argv[1:]
root = []
for opt in ('--root', '--ledger', '--history'):
    if opt in args:
        i = args.index(opt); root += [opt, args[i + 1]]; args = args[:i] + args[i + 2:]
L = ['python3', '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/ledger.py']
def run(cmd):
    r = subprocess.run(L + cmd + root, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode: sys.exit(f'refused: {" ".join(cmd[:2])}\n{r.stdout}{r.stderr}')
    return r.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1] if r.stdout.strip() else ''
n = 0
for d in args:
    p = os.path.join(d, 'final.rewrite')
    if os.path.exists(p):
        for line in open(p):
            m = re.match(r'\| *(\d+) *\|', line)
            if not m: continue
            with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', suffix='.row', delete=False) as f: f.write(line)
            print(run(['rewrite', m.group(1), f.name])); os.unlink(f.name); n += 1
    p = os.path.join(d, 'final.closes')
    if os.path.exists(p):
        for line in open(p):
            c = line.rstrip('\n').split('\t')
            if len(c) < 3 or not c[0].strip().isdigit(): continue
            cmd = ['close', c[0], '--commit', c[1], '--test', c[2]] + (['--note', c[3]] if len(c) > 3 and c[3] else [])
            print(run(cmd)); n += 1
print(f'apply.py: {n} changes')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

A `noted` block, which `note` writes, leaves the entry as it is. It adds what
the entry's history lacks, such as the curator's messages behind a text kept
word for word, with their times, or a correction of an earlier block. It holds
no earlier line, and its note says what it adds, so it needs one. A gone entry
takes none: its last block stays `merged into` or `removed`. A noted block
that corrects an earlier block names it by its time, in the field after the
kind: `correcting the block of 2026-10-13 19:07Z`, or, where blocks of the
entry share that minute, `correcting the 2nd block of 2026-10-14 04:41Z`,
counted oldest first. The block corrected is never edited.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`; for a noted block, no `--note`), a correction that
names no block or more than one, two blocks for one entry in one call.
Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the record file and its
history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:
  resolves one), --commit HASH (in HEAD's history), --by WHO, --note WHY.
  Each write needs --from or --note.

  add F|P --section TITLE FILE   a new entry from FILE's one line, numbered
      record.py add F --section 'Landed semantics' new.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The fix' --by coordinator
  set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] entry N rewritten from FILE's line, or moved
      record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'
  merge N --into M [FILE]        N removed, M rewritten from FILE (or kept),
                                 every pointer to N made a pointer to M
      record.py merge F-90 --into F-87 f87.md --note 'one fact, two entries'
  remove N                       N removed; refused while a pointer to it remains
      record.py remove P-131 --note 'evicted to the coordinator skill, references/briefing.md'
  note N [--correcting TIME]     a noted block in N's history, N unchanged; needs
                                 --note; refused when the history holds it already.
                                 TIME: 2026-10-13 19:07Z, or 2nd 2026-10-14 04:41Z
      record.py note P-25 --from 'positions-audit/full/evidence/corrections-c1.md#History lines the tool cannot write' --note 'his message behind the text: 2026-09-26T08:01:03.475Z, ...'
      record.py note P-7 --correcting '2026-10-13 19:07Z' --commit b87a17de5 --note 'that block names bc8902f47, ...'
  apply FILE                     many changes from one file, all or none (below)
      record.py apply chunk3.md --by 'consolidation chunk 3'
  check [--base COMMIT]          the store's checks; exit 1 on a failure
      record.py check --base cc9424c2a

An apply file holds, in any order: `## TITLE` or `### TITLE`, the section the
new entries below it go to (an existing entry stands under no heading, or
under its own section's, or the `## ` one that holds it); entry lines as they
should stand, `- F-87 ...`, or `- F-?1 ...` for a new entry, its placeholder
replaced by its number everywhere in the file; `move F-87 to SECTION`;
